newsitem.title: UK: BA lifts European fares 2.5 pct as fuel costs soar.
newsitem.headline: BA lifts European fares 2.5 pct as fuel costs soar.

text.p: British Airways Plc said on Wednesday it was increasing full published fares on its European routes by 2.5 percent on average from the middle of October.
BA said the rise in Europe was a direct consequence of the soaring cost of jet fuel, which has risen by 30 percent since the middle of July, and was considering increases on long-haul routes.
"We have been forced to file a number of fare increases recently, primarily as a result of the leaping cost of aviation fuel," a BA spokesman told Reuters.
The decision to increase European fares with effect from mid-October was taken within the last week or so and could be followed by further rises, he said.
"We're still evaluating a lot of routes... but the first move is in Europe. We are keeping a close check on the market," he added.

Jet fuel on the European spot market has risen by 30 percent since mid-July as world oil prices rocketed on a bullish cocktail of Middle East tension, low stocks and strong demand in the approach to winter.
Jet was trading at $266 a tonne on Wednesday, compared with $175 a tonne this time last year.
